key_insight: A spectral interface model captures fluid-fluid displacement dynamics in rough fractures beyond the quasistatic limit, showing that viscosity mainly changes relaxation time rather than the total energy dissipated.
engineering_relevance: The method enables efficient prediction of hysteresis and dissipation in heterogeneous fractures and porous media, supporting improved design and upscaling in flow, storage, and recovery applications.
method: Spectral computational approach for evolving fluid interfaces in an imperfect Hele-Shaw cell.
Tracks energy dissipation across metastable states and Haines jumps.
Validates against CFD simulations and experiments, including single-defect and random-roughness cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation by comparison with computational fluid dynamics simulations and experiments, and demonstrates dynamics over many orders of magnitude in time.
watch_item: The approach still depends on simplified fracture geometry, so extending it to fully realistic 3D porous media may require additional model calibration and computational care.
paper_title: Dynamics of fluid-fluid displacements in a model rough fracture beyond the quasistatic limit: A spectral approach
